trap_ledger.why: Brightpath has the lowest premium and PlanCompass's lowest estimate for Rosa, but the estimate is on a stale list (Pramitel, stopped in September; no Velmora) at ValueMart. At Corner Pharmacy, out of Brightpath's network, every fill is cash and Velmora is not on its formulary: $9,062 for the year. Choosing on the premium alone
Keystone covers all of Rosa's drugs with no prior authorization, but its $79 premium makes her year $2,076, $468 more than Northstar, where her doctor will send the authorization
Brightpath's premium is $4.20, but Corner Pharmacy is out of its network and Respiva is not on its formulary: $5,066 for Henrik's year
Northstar suits Rosa, but it leaves Henrik's Respiva inhaler off the formulary, $395 a fill in cash, $5,052 for his year
Enrolling in a new plan ends Rxmeadow on 1 January by itself (42 CFR 423.32(e)); disenrolling now ends Rosa's coverage on 30 November, leaving December with no drug plan, Velmora included
Henrik's Rxmeadow coverage ends by itself when Keystone starts on 1 January; disenrolling now leaves him without drug coverage in December
Rosa no longer drives and gets home delivery from Corner Pharmacy, which is preferred in the plan chosen for her: moving her prescriptions to ValueMart chases a premium, not her real pharmacy
Henrik gets home delivery from Corner Pharmacy, preferred in Keystone: moving his prescriptions serves no plan chosen for him
